card.name: Mukudj
card.tagline: Punu white-mask stilt dance honoring female ancestors
card.profile: Mukudj (also okuyi, mokuyi, mukudji) is the masquerade dance of the Punu (Bapunu) people of southern Gabon's Ngounie and Nyanga river region, performed with white kaolin-coated masks depicting idealized female ancestral faces (Punu-Lumbo mask, Wikipedia; Metropolitan Museum). Masks are crafted and danced by male members of the Mwiri men's society. Virtuosic male dancers wear the mask atop tall stilts, dressed in raffia and skins, executing acrobatic choreography at funerals, births, initiations and other major events to invoke ancestral approval (Met Museum). The white color, from riverbed kaolin, symbolizes beauty, the afterlife and the spirits of the dead; diamond and square scarification motifs evoke Punu women and the people's nine primordial clans.
card.insight: Punu white masks were among the first African artworks to win recognition from early-20th-century European modern artists, who wrongly speculated about Asian influence though the form is indigenous to southern Gabon (Metropolitan Museum); masks are treated respectfully as ancestral spirit objects.
